title: Study notes
html:
The technique toolbox

  • Ultrasound: first-line for size, hydronephrosis, cysts vs solid, bladder, children and pregnancy; does not see the normal ureter and misses ureteral stones.
  • Non-contrast CT: gold standard for stones (almost all hyperdense, including uric acid) and renal colic.
  • Multiphase contrast CT: renal masses (nephrographic phase), staging, trauma (stable patient), CT urography for the urothelium.
  • KUB: radio-opaque stones (90 %), nephrocalcinosis, follow-up. IVU: historical – nephrogram → pyelogram at 5 and 15 min; "mute kidney" = no excretion at 5 AND 15 min.
  • MRI: masses when contrast CT is impossible; scintigraphy: function (see Techniques); cystography: reflux, bladder rupture.

Obstruction and stones

Hydronephrosis = dilated pelvis and calyces (grades I–IV); find the level: UPJ (dilated pelvis, thin ureter), ureter (stone, stricture, tumour), bladder outlet (both sides + thick bladder). A stone is hyperechoic with a shadow on US, hyperdense on CT; uric acid stones are lucent on X-ray. Staghorn = cast of the pelvis and calyces.

Renal masses

  • Simple cyst (Bosniak I): anechoic, thin wall, enhancement behind; CT 0–20 HU, no enhancement. Higher Bosniak = septa, calcification, enhancing parts → IIF follow-up, III/IV surgery.
  • Renal cell carcinoma: solid enhancing mass, often heterogeneous; stage with CT (renal vein and IVC thrombus, nodes, adrenal, lung).
  • Angiomyolipoma: macroscopic fat → the only renal tumour diagnosed with near-certainty by US + CT.
  • Urothelial carcinoma: filling defect in the collecting system, multicentric – CT urography.
  • Wilms: child, large solid mass with claw sign. Polycystic disease: large kidneys with countless cysts.

Bladder

  • Compensated stasis ("fighting bladder"): detrusor hypertrophy, thick trabeculated wall, small diverticula.
  • Decompensated: large atonic thin-walled bladder, large diverticula, residue, upper-tract dilatation.
  • Tumour = fixed, vascular wall mass; clot = mobile, avascular; stone = mobile, shadowing.

Exam reflexes

  • Corticomedullary differentiation = arterial phase; homogeneous = nephrographic phase.
  • Small kidney is never due to hydronephrosis, tumour or acute disease.
  • US cannot rule out a ureteral stone.
